Run pinned offline microsandbox-filesystem mount_policy tests in an xattr-capable scratch environment; then a direct isolated guest probe must pass the positive control and fail nonzero on forbidden listing/read. title: ensure-images: keep eval-error fail-closed vs nix-absent trust posture — document decision
description:
Objective: record and document the decision to KEEP the ensure-images fail-closed posture on nix eval errors, distinct from the nix-absent trust posture. This is a documentation/decision bead — no code change.

Decision (recorded 2026-08-03):
- Eval errors (nix build fails to evaluate the image drvPath) → FAIL-CLOSED: surface the eval error and refuse up/exec. Rationale: an eval error almost always conceals a real config bug (a missing attr, a broken overlay, a stale lock), so trusting past it would silently run a stale/foreign image. The operator must fix the config.
- nix-absent (the `nix` binary is unavailable, e.g. a standalone install with no nix) → TRUST posture: ensure-images degrades to trusting the msb image store and only forces a build/load when a tag is absent. This is the documented standalone-install path (spec 21 §3.4 skew matrix, §8).
- Tag-absent (nix present or absent) → ALWAYS forces a build/load; never trusted.

The two postures are deliberately different: eval-error is a CONFIG signal (fix the config), nix-absent is an ENVIRONMENT signal (no nix to evaluate with). Conflating them would either mask config bugs (if eval-error trusted) or break standalone installs (if nix-absent fail-closed). The current code keeps them separate; this bead records the rationale so a future refactor does not collapse them.

Related spec: 21-image-build-lifecycle.md §3 (change detection — the eval-only drvPath signal), §3.4 (skew matrix), §8 (state schema). Cross-ref: this decision is noted in spec 21 §15 open follow-ups.

title: Canonical config-flake input URL (Phase-5 decision)
description:

Push-state check (host): run `git -C <workestrate-checkout> fetch && git log --oneline origin/migration/tool-model..HEAD` to confirm whether the local HEAD (ddff1a0 + the host-boot fix commits) is pushed. If unpushed commits exist, push before adopting the github: input, then relock with `nix flake lock --update-input workestrate` on the host.

Supersedes: the `git+file:///home/rybski/...` host-path workaround (a Phase-5 decision will retire it). Related spec: 21-image-build-lifecycle.md (the config-flake input is what makes the nix-layered image builds reproducible across machines — see §10 phased plan and §12.3 migration notes).

title: Revisit short_msb_home / KVM-test MSB_HOME convention for a more idiomatic approach
description: Objective: the short_msb_home() fixed-/tmp helper + the MSB_HOME-vs-HOME decoupling in the two KVM tests (lifecycle_detached.rs, ensure_images_e2e.rs) is a pragmatic workaround for the 108-byte unix-socket limit (MSB_HOME/run/agent/<32hex>.sock = len+48 < 108 => len(MSB_HOME) <= 59). Brainstorm a more idiomatic long-term approach and refactor. Options: (a) msb supporting a configurable run/socket dir via paths.sandboxes (or equivalent) so the socket path is independent of MSB_HOME depth; (b) a canonical short-MSB_HOME test convention surfaced as a first-class test-support helper with a documented contract, rather than a /tmp literal in two KVM tests. Either path lets the KVM tests return to the temp_dir() idiom and removes the /tmp divergence (documented on the helper). Acceptance: a chosen approach is recorded, the /tmp literal is removed or justified, and the KVM tests still pass on a HOST-KVM host. Environment: HOST-KVM (validation) + verifiable-here (refactor).
